task.title: Production Neon Auth branch does not trust any localhost origin, blocking release desktop sign-in by default
task.description:
Discovered while verifying WB-01M036CA3M185WM4WGS5SDC161 (2026-08-16): that task
fixed the code-side bug where account::sign_in/sign_up/etc. sent the untrusted
127.0.0.1 origin under Tauri release desktop instead of the localhost spelling
google_sign_in already preferred (cookies::request_origin now overrides via
native::embedded_origin() for every caller).

That fix is necessary but NOT sufficient to close the maintainer's originally
reported symptom. Live probe of the already-built release .app
(target/release/bundle/macos/three-rings.app), launched exactly as Finder would
(no exported env — src-tauri/src/lib.rs defaults NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL to the
PRODUCTION Neon Auth branch when unset, since "packaged release apps ... receive
no shell environment"):

- Against the DEV branch (NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL exported explicitly): bad-credential
  /api/sign_in correctly returns "Invalid email or password" and /api/google_sign_in
  returns a valid social-init URL, regardless of the curl request's own Host header
  (127.0.0.1 or localhost) — proves the code fix works.
- Against the PRODUCTION branch (the release app's actual default): /api/sign_in
  still returns the literal upstream "Invalid origin", and /api/google_sign_in still
  returns INVALID_CALLBACKURL/403 — i.e. the maintainer's exact originally-reported
  symptom persists even with the code fix applied.

Root cause: per specs/auth.md's 2026-08-15 Findings entry, production Neon Auth
keeps "Allow Localhost" off entirely (unlike dev, which has allow_localhost=true).
The code fix makes the app present the *correctly-spelled* trusted origin
(http://localhost:<port>, not the untrusted 127.0.0.1 spelling), but production
still refuses it outright because it does not trust ANY loopback origin — spelling
was never the issue there.

To do: a maintainer decision + Neon Auth console change on the PRODUCTION branch
— either enable allow_localhost (mirroring dev) or add an explicit trusted-origins
allowance that covers the release desktop app's dynamic loopback port. Explicitly
out of scope for WB-01M036CA3M185WM4WGS5SDC161 (constraint: no Neon Auth config
changes). See specs/auth.md Findings (2026-08-16 entry) for the full probe
transcript and reasoning.
